{
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "sentry-repo",
      "line": 1,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Accidental submodule committed",
      "body": "This PR adds a git submodule named 'sentry-repo' pointing at a commit. That appears unintentional and can break clones, CI, or repository layout. Remove the submodule/gitlink before merging."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_events_stats.py",
      "line": 220,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Upsampling eligibility uses outer dataset instead of the dataset actually queried",
      "body": "_get_event_stats receives scoped_dataset, but eligibility is computed with the outer 'dataset' variable. In dashboard-split/fallback paths _get_event_stats can be called with a different dataset (e.g. discover), so the decision to transform count() can be based on the wrong dataset. This can skip upsampling or apply it inconsistently."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py",
      "line": 137,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Error-focused query detection is a naive substring check",
      "body": "_is_error_focused_query returns true whenever 'event.type:error' appears in the raw request query. This matches negated clauses such as '!event.type:error', mixed queries like 'event.type:error OR event.type:transaction', and text inside quoted values. It also fails to treat '!event.type:transaction' as error-focused. Since this controls whether count() is replaced by sum(sample_weight), it can apply weights to non-error events or miss error-only queries, producing incorrect counts. Parse the search syntax or use the final query string instead."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py",
      "line": 38,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Eligibility cache can serve stale allowlist decisions and has no wired invalidation",
      "body": "Allowlist eligibility is cached for 60 seconds, but invalidate_upsampling_cache is never called when the 'issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist' option changes. If the allowlist is updated, queries can continue using the old upsampling decision for up to a minute, returning incorrect counts. Include a config version in the cache key or invoke invalidation on option changes."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py",
      "line": 27,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Cache key uses Python hash() of project IDs",
      "body": "The cache key embeds hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids))). Tuple hashes can collide and are not a stable, collision-safe identifier for cached correctness. A collision between different project sets could reuse an eligibility decision for the wrong projects. Use a deterministic unique key such as joined sorted project IDs or a stable hash."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py",
      "line": 92,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "Only literal count() is transformed and aliasing is forced",
      "body": "The transform only rewrites columns that exactly match 'count()' after lower/strip and rewrites them to 'upsampled_count() as count'. It does not handle aliased forms like 'count() as total', other count variants, or equations. This can leave some count aggregations unupsampled while changing the output alias for others, causing inconsistent API responses for clients expecting the original field name."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py",
      "line": 63,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "perf",
      "title": "Allowlist membership check uses list lookups",
      "body": "_are_all_projects_error_upsampled checks 'project_id in allowlist' where allowlist is a list. On a cache miss this is O(number of queried projects * allowlist size). Convert the allowlist to a set before checking membership."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py",
      "line": 1041,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "upsampled_count is exposed as a public query function",
      "body": "The new upsampled_count SnQL function is added without private=True, unlike neighboring internal functions. This may allow API callers to invoke it directly in queries, bypassing the allowlist/error-upsampling checks and potentially exposing sample-weight-derived counts. Mark the function private or gate it appropriately."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py",
      "line": 1048,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "upsampled_count does not handle missing/null sample weights",
      "body": "The aggregate is toInt64(sum(sample_weight)). If any event in an allowlisted project has a NULL or unpopulated sample_weight (for example historical events before upsampling metadata existed), those events can contribute zero or nothing to the sum, causing severe undercounting. Use coalesce(sample_weight, 1) or another explicit default unless the schema guarantees a non-NULL weight of 1 for every row."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py",
      "line": 1047,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "toInt64 truncates fractional upsampled sums",
      "body": "sample_weight values can be fractional, and sum(sample_weight) may therefore be fractional. Wrapping it in toInt64 truncates rather than rounding, biasing the estimated error count downward. Consider rounding or returning a numeric/float result."
    },
    {
      "file": "tests/snuba/api/endpoints/test_organization_events_stats.py",
      "line": 3605,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "Endpoint tests do not clear or test the upsampling eligibility cache",
      "body": "The tests patch the allowlist option but do not clear the 'error_upsampling_eligible:*' cache entries. Since the eligibility cache lives for 60 seconds, a value cached by one test can affect later tests with the same organization/project IDs, making the suite order-dependent and preventing validation of stale-cache behavior. Clear the cache in setUp or add explicit cache invalidation/staleness tests."
    },
    {
      "file": "tests/snuba/api/endpoints/test_organization_events_stats.py",
      "line": 3554,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "Missing coverage for key upsampling paths",
      "body": "The new tests only cover simple stats requests with 'event.type:error'. They do not cover the errors dataset, top-events paths, RPC paths, aliased/equation count columns, dashboard split queries, or mixed/negated event.type queries. These are the paths where the transform is applied and are likely to regress."
    }
  ]
}

findings.title: Accidental submodule committed
findings.body: This PR adds a git submodule named 'sentry-repo' pointing at a commit. That appears unintentional and can break clones, CI, or repository layout. Remove the submodule/gitlink before merging.

findings.title: Upsampling eligibility uses outer dataset instead of the dataset actually queried
findings.body: _get_event_stats receives scoped_dataset, but eligibility is computed with the outer 'dataset' variable. In dashboard-split/fallback paths _get_event_stats can be called with a different dataset (e.g. discover), so the decision to transform count() can be based on the wrong dataset. This can skip upsampling or apply it inconsistently.

findings.title: Error-focused query detection is a naive substring check
findings.body: _is_error_focused_query returns true whenever 'event.type:error' appears in the raw request query. This matches negated clauses such as '!event.type:error', mixed queries like 'event.type:error OR event.type:transaction', and text inside quoted values. It also fails to treat '!event.type:transaction' as error-focused. Since this controls whether count() is replaced by sum(sample_weight), it can apply weights to non-error events or miss error-only queries, producing incorrect counts. Parse the search syntax or use the final query string instead.

findings.title: Eligibility cache can serve stale allowlist decisions and has no wired invalidation
findings.body: Allowlist eligibility is cached for 60 seconds, but invalidate_upsampling_cache is never called when the 'issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist' option changes. If the allowlist is updated, queries can continue using the old upsampling decision for up to a minute, returning incorrect counts. Include a config version in the cache key or invoke invalidation on option changes.

findings.title: Cache key uses Python hash() of project IDs
findings.body: The cache key embeds hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids))). Tuple hashes can collide and are not a stable, collision-safe identifier for cached correctness. A collision between different project sets could reuse an eligibility decision for the wrong projects. Use a deterministic unique key such as joined sorted project IDs or a stable hash.

findings.title: Only literal count() is transformed and aliasing is forced
findings.body: The transform only rewrites columns that exactly match 'count()' after lower/strip and rewrites them to 'upsampled_count() as count'. It does not handle aliased forms like 'count() as total', other count variants, or equations. This can leave some count aggregations unupsampled while changing the output alias for others, causing inconsistent API responses for clients expecting the original field name.

findings.title: Allowlist membership check uses list lookups
findings.body: _are_all_projects_error_upsampled checks 'project_id in allowlist' where allowlist is a list. On a cache miss this is O(number of queried projects * allowlist size). Convert the allowlist to a set before checking membership.

findings.title: upsampled_count is exposed as a public query function
findings.body: The new upsampled_count SnQL function is added without private=True, unlike neighboring internal functions. This may allow API callers to invoke it directly in queries, bypassing the allowlist/error-upsampling checks and potentially exposing sample-weight-derived counts. Mark the function private or gate it appropriately.

findings.title: upsampled_count does not handle missing/null sample weights
findings.body: The aggregate is toInt64(sum(sample_weight)). If any event in an allowlisted project has a NULL or unpopulated sample_weight (for example historical events before upsampling metadata existed), those events can contribute zero or nothing to the sum, causing severe undercounting. Use coalesce(sample_weight, 1) or another explicit default unless the schema guarantees a non-NULL weight of 1 for every row.

findings.title: toInt64 truncates fractional upsampled sums
findings.body: sample_weight values can be fractional, and sum(sample_weight) may therefore be fractional. Wrapping it in toInt64 truncates rather than rounding, biasing the estimated error count downward. Consider rounding or returning a numeric/float result.

findings.title: Endpoint tests do not clear or test the upsampling eligibility cache
findings.body: The tests patch the allowlist option but do not clear the 'error_upsampling_eligible:*' cache entries. Since the eligibility cache lives for 60 seconds, a value cached by one test can affect later tests with the same organization/project IDs, making the suite order-dependent and preventing validation of stale-cache behavior. Clear the cache in setUp or add explicit cache invalidation/staleness tests.

findings.title: Missing coverage for key upsampling paths
findings.body: The new tests only cover simple stats requests with 'event.type:error'. They do not cover the errors dataset, top-events paths, RPC paths, aliased/equation count columns, dashboard split queries, or mixed/negated event.type queries. These are the paths where the transform is applied and are likely to regress.
